literature.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 残基 45 和 144 处存在低糖基化并不影响细胞培养物中的病毒生长,但它降低了小鼠体内与病毒中和和预防流感疾病相关的抗体滴度。 [10.1128/jvi.00662-26]
经常报道的流感 疫苗接种 的动机是属于风险群体和降低流感风险。对安全性和不良反应的担忧是常见的障碍。接种了 COVID-19 疫苗的个体更有可能感染流感 疫苗接种,反之亦然,表明 疫苗 摄取这两种病原体之间存在潜在关联。 [10.64898/2026.08.25.26361301]
Twitter/X数据推导出的估计值落在中期报告的范围内,表明该方法可作为当前疫苗有效性(VE)估计系统的补充。 [10.64898/2026.08.28.26361670]
该研究强调,马流感病毒为流感病毒生态学、进化 和 宿主 相互作用提供了重要见解,特别是由于其独特的流行病学特征类似于人类 季节性流感 病毒。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551]
在流感感染期间,病毒诱导的葡萄糖、脂质、氨基酸和嘌呤代谢的改变导致代谢中间体的异常积累,这与细胞能量稳态破坏、炎症和免疫应答改变以及可能稳定病理表型的潜在表观遗传修饰有关。 [10.1016/j.pharmthera.2026.109105]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。

key_findings_en: The presence of low glycosylation at residues 45 and 144 did not affect virus growth in cell culture, but it reduced antibody titers in mice that correlate with virus neutralization and protection against influenza disease. [10.1128/jvi.00662-26]

Belonging to a risk group and reducing the risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination. Concerns about safety and adverse effects were common barriers. [10.64898/2026.08.25.26361301]
The estimates derived from the Twitter/X data fell within the range of interim reports, indicating that the method could complement current systems for VE estimation. [10.64898/2026.08.28.26361670]

The study highlights that equine influenza virus has provided critical insights into influenza virus ecology, evolution, and host interactions, particularly due to its unique epidemiological characteristics resembling those of human seasonal influenza viruses. [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551]

news.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 由于季节性流感,贾坎德邦已进入戒备状态,医院准备设立隔离病房。 [news-cf017534dab116ed]
世卫组织已发布有关 H5N1 病毒的警报,由于印度同时与 季节性流感 A(H1N1) 和禽流感 暴发 作斗争,该病毒变得越来越紧迫。该警报是基于 H5N1 在鸟类中的持续传播以及动物向人类 跨物种溢出 的可能性。 [news-9791bc6c1d2321bc]
香港推出了 2026-27 年 季节性流感 疫苗接种 计划,比上一年提前一周开始。政府对 疫苗 采购进行了多元化,并简化了行政措施,以促进早期 疫苗接种 的实施。该事件的确认基于官方声明和政策变化。 [news-da4ee55e09d0025b]
卫生防护中心 (CHP) 警告学生返校时可能出现流感 暴发,理由是流感活动有所增加。自六月底进入流感季节以来,卫生防护中心报告了11宗严重小儿流感感染个案。在这些年轻患者中,两人情况危急,一人死亡。 [news-0d44721e40146755]
本季,德里的 H1N1 病例急剧增加,该病毒占甲型流感病例的最大比例。专家表示,这种增加似乎与新的或异常危险的毒株无关,并且正在传播的病毒显示出与正常 季节性流感 一致的变化。 [news-5deb4570d49824d8]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Seasonal influenza viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: Jharkhand has been placed on alert due to seasonal influenza, with hospitals preparing to set up isolation wards. [news-cf017534dab116ed]

WHO has issued an alert about the H5N1 virus, which is gaining urgency due to India's simultaneous battle with seasonal influenza A(H1N1) and avian influenza outbreaks. The alert is based on the ongoing spread of H5N1 among birds and the potential for animal-to-human spillover. [news-9791bc6c1d2321bc]

Hong Kong has launched a seasonal influenza vaccination programme for 2026-27, starting one week earlier than the previous year. The government has diversified vaccine procurement and streamlined administrative measures to facilitate early vaccination. [news-da4ee55e09d0025b]

The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) warned of potential flu outbreaks as students return to school, citing an increase in influenza activity. The CHP reported 11 cases of severe paediatric influenza infection since the city entered the influenza season in late June. [news-0d44721e40146755]

H1N1 cases have risen sharply in Delhi this season, with the virus accounting for the largest share of influenza A cases. Experts have stated that the increase does not appear to be linked to a new or unusually dangerous strain, and the circulating virus shows changes consistent with normal seasonal influenza. [news-5deb4570d49824d8]

papers.title: Factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants, 2023-2025.
papers.abstract: Seasonal Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination programmes are critical for reducing morbidity and mortality in older adults, yet uptake remains uneven across populations. We aimed to profile vaccination attitudes and examine predictors of COVID-19/influenza vaccination uptake among a UK participatory surveillance system - FluSurvey. We analysed FluSurvey data from participants aged [≥]65 years who were eligible for both vaccines in the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn - Winter seasonal campaigns. Descriptive analyses examined self-reported attitudes to influenza vaccination. Logistic regression examined factors (age, sex, socioeconomic status, education, employment, transport, smoking and chronic conditions) associated with influenza and COVID-19 vaccination uptake in each season, adjusting for confounders. Belonging to a risk group and reducing risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination, while building natural immunity and concerns around safety and adverse effects were frequently reported barriers. Individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination (aOR2023-2024=13.90 [9.28-21.17]; aOR2024-2025=8.54 [5.82-12.60]), and vice-versa (aOR2023-2024=13.91 [9.30-21.19]; aOR2024-2025=8.52 [5.81-12.58]). Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of COVID-19 vaccination (aOR2023-2024=0.59 [0.45-0.78], aOR2024-2025: 0.56 [0.39-0.79]). Other results were weaker or demonstrated variation by season. Our findings highlight recent attitudes and barriers to influenza and COVID-19 vaccination among the FluSurvey cohort, which may inform approaches to improve vaccination coverage in the population.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants aged ≥65 years during the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn-Winter campaigns. The review finds that individuals vaccinated against one pathogen are more likely to receive the other, but other factors show weaker or inconsistent associations. It highlights the need for targeted strategies to improve vaccination coverage and suggests further research to address seasonal variations and evidence gaps in understanding vaccine behavior.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 季节性流感 病毒,特别研究了 2023-2024 年和 2024-2025 年秋冬季运动期间英国流感调查参与者中与 季节性流感 和 SARS-CoV-2 相关的 疫苗接种 相关因素。核心问题是分析 疫苗接种 态度并确定两种病原体 疫苗 摄取的预测因子。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述分析了年龄≥65岁且符合 疫苗 资格的参与者的流感调查数据。使用逻辑回归来检查与流感和 COVID-19 疫苗接种 摄取相关的因素(年龄、性别、社会经济地位、教育、就业、交通、吸烟和慢性病),并调整混杂因素。进行描述性分析以探讨自我报告的对流感 疫苗接种 的态度。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 经常报道的流感 疫苗接种 的动机是属于风险群体和降低流感风险。对安全性和不良反应的担忧是常见的障碍。接种了 COVID-19 疫苗的个体更有可能感染流感 疫苗接种,反之亦然,表明 疫苗 摄取这两种病原体之间存在潜在关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 较低的教育程度与较低的 COVID-19 疫苗接种 几率相关。其他结果较弱或随季节变化而变化,表明研究结果的一致性有限。该综述没有提供有关目标与相关实体之间的生物学或分类学关系的详细信息,也没有解决理解这些关系方面的具体差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调了流感调查 队列研究 中最近对流感和 COVID-19 疫苗接种 的态度和障碍,这可能为提高 疫苗接种 在人群中覆盖率的策略提供参考。需要进一步的研究来探索 疫苗 吸收的季节性变化,并解决在理解影响 疫苗接种 行为的因素方面的证据差距。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 较低的教育程度与较低的 COVID-19 疫苗接种 几率相关。其他结果较弱或随季节变化而变化,表明研究结果的一致性有限。该综述没有提供有关目标与相关实体之间的生物学或分类学关系的详细信息,也没有解决理解这些关系方面的具体差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调了流感调查 队列研究 中最近对流感和 COVID-19 疫苗接种 的态度和障碍,这可能为提高 疫苗接种 在人群中覆盖率的策略提供参考。需要进一步的研究来探索 疫苗 吸收的季节性变化,并解决在理解影响 疫苗接种 行为的因素方面的证据差距。

papers.title: N-linked glycosylation sites with low occupancy support sustained circulation of the A(H3N2) influenza A virus in the human population.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Glycosylation of the influenza A virus hemagglutinin is crucial for viral fitness and immune evasion. The hemagglutinin of contemporary human A(H3N2) influenza A viruses is extensively glycosylated with up to 13 putative glycosylation sites. Glycan types and occupancy of these sites are not uniform: while most are nearly completely occupied by glycans, some, such as those at amino acid residues 45 and 144, are only partially occupied and are evolutionarily unstable. While the effects of highly occupied glycosylated sites of hemagglutinin on A(H3N2) influenza A virus biology are well studied, there is limited information on the functional impact of the low-occupancy glycosylation sites on the viral hemagglutinin. Here, by using reverse-genetics A(H3N2) influenza A viruses lacking glycans at either residue 45 or 144, or both in hemagglutinin, we demonstrate that, despite reduced receptor binding, thermal stability, and fusion, the presence of a low level of glycosylation at these positions does not impact virus growth in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial cell culture. In contrast, these low-occupancy sites do affect immune responses in mice, by reducing titers of antibodies that correlate with virus neutralization and protection against influenza disease. We suggest that the temporary introduction of sites with low glycosylation allows influenza viruses to reduce the immune pressure on antigenic and receptor binding sites of hemagglutinin without significantly compromising viral virulence. This mechanism may help support the sustained circulation of A(H3N2) influenza A virus in human populations. IMPORTANCE Many of the glycosylation sites on the hemagglutinin of influenza A viruses are near antigenic sites, such that the glycans block antibody recognition and help evade population immunity. However, glycans may also reduce viral replication and virulence. Glycosylation sites at amino acid residues 45 and 144 of the hemagglutinin of contemporary A(H3N2) influenza A viruses are minimally occupied, with fewer than 10% of the sites containing glycans. This is still sufficient to partially evade antibody-based population immunity, while minimizing the impact on replication and virulence. Over time, A(H3N2) viruses have used both these sites only during limited periods, suggesting that even a low level of glycan occupancy may confer some negative selection pressure that is compensated by evasion of human population immunity. Data from this study provide a better understanding of the mechanisms that allow viruses to evade antibody-based immunity and maintain circulation in the human population. However, glycans may also reduce viral replication and virulence.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the functional impact of low-occupancy glycosylation sites on the hemagglutinin of A(H3N2) influenza A viruses and their role in immune evasion and viral persistence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved reverse-genetics to generate A(H3N2) influenza A viruses lacking glycans at specific hemagglutinin residues, and tested these viruses in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial cell culture and in mice.
analysis.methods: The researchers used reverse-genetics to create A(H3N2) influenza A viruses with modified glycosylation sites at residues 45 and 144, and assessed their effects on viral growth in cell culture and immune responses in mice.
analysis.main_results: The presence of low glycosylation at residues 45 and 144 did not affect virus growth in cell culture, but it reduced antibody titers in mice that correlate with virus neutralization and protection against influenza disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that low-occupancy glycosylation sites may help influenza viruses reduce immune pressure on key antigenic sites without significantly compromising virulence, offering a novel insight into viral immune evasion strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform strategies for vaccine design and surveillance by highlighting the role of low-occupancy glycosylation sites in maintaining viral circulation and immune evasion in human populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and in vivo models, and the evidence is moderate as it does not include long-term population-level data or clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the functional impact of low-occupancy glycosylation sites on the hemagglutinin of A(H3N2) influenza A viruses. It demonstrates that despite reduced receptor binding and thermal stability, these sites do not hinder viral growth in cell culture. However, they do affect immune responses in mice by reducing antibody titers associated with neutralization and protection. The authors propose that these sites may help the virus evade immune pressure while maintaining virulence, supporting its sustained circulation in human populations. The study uses reverse-genetics and animal models, which provide moderate evidence but lack direct clinical data. These findings could inform vaccine development and surveillance strategies for seasonal influenza viruses.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及反向遗传学来生成在特定血凝素残基处缺乏聚糖的 甲型H3N2流感病毒 甲型流感病毒,并在 Madin-Darby 犬肾上皮细胞培养物和小鼠中测试了这些病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员利用反向遗传学创建了在残基 45 和 144 处糖基化位点经过修饰的 甲型H3N2流感病毒 甲型流感病毒,并评估了它们对细胞培养物中病毒生长和小鼠体内 免疫应答 的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 残基 45 和 144 处存在低糖基化并不影响细胞培养物中的病毒生长,但它降低了小鼠体内与病毒中和和预防流感疾病相关的抗体滴度。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,低占有率糖基化位点可能有助于流感病毒减少关键抗原位点的免疫压力,而不会显着损害毒力,从而为病毒免疫逃避策略提供了新的见解。

papers.title: Deciphering influenza B virus-derived peptides and their presentation by HLA class I molecules.
papers.abstract: Despite influenza vaccines being widely available, influenza still causes significant morbidity and mortality annually. Vaccines typically induce humoral-mediated protection against rapidly mutating surface glycoproteins, necessitating that they be updated and administered each year. In contrast, CD8+ T cells, which can control and clear viral infections, can recognise more conserved viral epitopes. Therefore, there is considerable interest in understanding CD8+ T cell responses to influenza virus for the development of future vaccines and therapeutics. Although Alphainfluenzavirus influenzae (FLUAV) and Betainfluenzavirus influenzae (FLUBV) co-circulate in humans and both contribute to seasonal epidemics, there is limited data regarding CD8+ T cell responses to FLUBV. This knowledge gap spans both immunological and molecular insights. In the present review, we summarise the current knowledge of FLUBV-derived CD8+ T cell epitopes at both cellular and molecular levels, in comparison with FLUAV. Collectively, this highlights the limited data available on FLUBV, despite its significant role in human influenza infections.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses human seasonal influenza B virus (FLUBV) with a focus on CD8+ T cell responses to conserved epitopes, contrasting with influenza A virus (FLUAV). It highlights that current vaccines, which induce humoral responses against rapidly mutating surface glycoproteins, require annual updates, whereas CD8+ T cells target more conserved epitopes, offering potential for broader protection. papers.title: Mechanisms of ‘metabolizeaccretion’ and therapeutic targets in influenza infection
papers.abstract: Influenza virus infection remains a leading cause of acute respiratory illness worldwide, with increasing resistance to conventional antiviral therapies highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. This review introduces the concept of metabolizeaccretion, a self-reinforcing pathological cascade driven by metabolic reprogramming and characterized by three progressive stages: trigger, amplification, and persistence. During influenza infection, viral-induced alterations in glucose, lipid, amino acid, and purine metabolism lead to the aberrant accumulation of metabolic intermediates, which are associated with disrupted cellular energy homeostasis, altered inflammatory and immune responses, and potential epigenetic modifications that may stabilize pathological phenotypes. These processes collectively effect viral replication, immune evasion, and progression to severe respiratory damage. We further discuss potential therapeutic interventions targeting key metabolic enzymes, accumulated metabolites, gene expression regulation, and specific receptors to disrupt metabolizeaccretion. Finally, we emphasize the importance of multi-target approaches and precision medicine strategies to address metabolic heterogeneity in lung microenvironments, offering new insights for the treatment and management of influenza and related respiratory diseases.

papers.title: Memory B Cell Repertoire of a Repeatedly Vaccinated Individual Includes Influenza Hemagglutinin-Specific Cross-Group Binders with Affinity Beyond A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H3N2) Seasonal Strains
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Humans are primarily infected by two distinct seasonal influenza A virus (IAV) subtypes, A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H3N2). Because IAV mutates rapidly, it continuously escapes existing protective antibodies. However, repeated exposure to these evolving strains increases the diversity of virus-specific memory B cell (MBC) population. To investigate the extent of this diversity and cross-reactivity of IAV- specific immunity in adults, and its possible impact on emerging strains, we analyzed the hemagglutinin (HA)-specific MBC repertoire of an adult frequently immunized with seasonal vaccines. Methods: High-throughput single-cell sequencing of HA probe-positive MBCs collected from an individual with repeated seasonal influenza vaccination was performed. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from multicell clonotypes were tested for HA binding and influenza virus neutralization. Results: Two clonotypes were identified that bound to both A(H1) and A(H3) HAs from strains circulating before and after the season of blood collection. Both clonotypes neutralized A(H3N2) strains, while one also neutralized A(H1N1)pdm09 strains. Notably, these cross-group binders showed affinity for A(H5), A(H7) and A(H9) avian influenza HAs and neutralized bovine A(H5N1) IAV. Conclusions: Our findings suggest that seasonal vaccination can support pre-existing cross-reactive B-cell immunity in some individuals. This underscores the importance of studying influenza-specific MBC repertoires across diverse populations to better understand immune dynamics and improve vaccine design.

papers.title_zh: 重复接种疫苗的个体的记忆 B 细胞库包括流感血凝素特异性跨群结合物,其亲和力超出 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 和 甲型H3N2流感病毒 季节性菌株
papers.source_body_en: Background/Objectives: Humans are primarily infected by two distinct seasonal influenza A virus (IAV) subtypes, A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H3N2). Because IAV mutates rapidly, it continuously escapes existing protective antibodies. However, repeated exposure to these evolving strains increases the diversity of virus-specific memory B cell (MBC) population. To investigate the extent of this diversity and cross-reactivity of IAV- specific immunity in adults, and its possible impact on emerging strains, we analyzed the hemagglutinin (HA)-specific MBC repertoire of an adult frequently immunized with seasonal vaccines. Methods: High-throughput single-cell sequencing of HA probe-positive MBCs collected from an individual with repeated seasonal influenza vaccination was performed. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from multicell clonotypes were tested for HA binding and influenza virus neutralization. Results: Two clonotypes were identified that bound to both A(H1) and A(H3) HAs from strains circulating before and after the season of blood collection. Both clonotypes neutralized A(H3N2) strains, while one also neutralized A(H1N1)pdm09 strains. Notably, these cross-group binders showed affinity for A(H5), A(H7) and A(H9) avian influenza HAs and neutralized bovine A(H5N1) IAV. Conclusions: Our findings suggest that seasonal vaccination can support pre-existing cross-reactive B-cell immunity in some individuals. This underscores the importance of studying influenza-specific MBC repertoires across diverse populations to better understand immune dynamics and improve vaccine design.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目标:人类主要感染两种不同的 季节性流感 A 病毒 (IAV) 亚型:甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 和 甲型H3N2流感病毒。由于 IAV 突变迅速,它会不断逃避现有的保护性抗体。然而,反复接触这些不断进化的毒株会增加病毒特异性记忆 B 细胞 (MBC) 群体的多样性。为了调查成人 IAV 特异性免疫的多样性和交叉反应性程度,及其对新出现菌株的可能影响,我们分析了经常接受季节性 疫苗 免疫的成人的血凝素 (HA) 特异性 MBC 库。方法:对从重复 季节性流感 疫苗接种 的个体收集的 HA 探针阳性 MBC 进行高通量单细胞测序。测试了来自多细胞克隆型的单克隆抗体 (mAb) 的 HA 结合和流感病毒中和作用。结果:鉴定出两种克隆型,它们与采血季前后循环菌株中的 A(H1) 和 A(H3) HA 结合。两种克隆型均中和 甲型H3N2流感病毒 菌株,而其中一种也中和 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 菌株。值得注意的是,这些跨基团结合剂表现出对 A(H5)、A(H7) 和 A(H9) 禽流感 HA 以及中和牛 A(H5N1) IAV 的亲和力。结论:我们的研究结果表明,季节性 疫苗接种 可以支持某些个体预先存在的交叉反应 B 细胞免疫。这强调了研究不同人群的流感特异性 MBC 库的重要性,以更好地了解免疫动态并改进 疫苗 设计。

papers.title: Influenza A virus H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 show temperature-dependent restriction of replication in primary human respiratory epithelial cell cultures derived from the upper and lower respiratory tract.
papers.abstract: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b avian influenza A viruses pose a significant threat to wild animal populations, domesticated animals, and potentially, the human population. For H5N1s to infect and transmit among mammalian species, mutations for improved utilization of mammalian receptors and enhanced replication at the lower temperatures of the upper respiratory tract need to be acquired. A human H1N1pdm09-like virus was compared to H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 for replication at 33{o}C, 37{o}C, and 39{o}C - temperatures consistent with the upper and lower respiratory tract in humans, and dairy cow udder tissue. All H5N1 viruses had increased plaque sizes on MDCK cells at 37{o}C and 39{o}C compared to H1N1pdm09. In primary, differentiated human nasal and bronchial epithelial cultures, all H5N1 viruses show restricted infectious virus production compared to H1N1 at 33{o}C. While H5N1 D1.1 also showed restricted replication at 37{o}C and 39{o}C, the H5N1 B3.13 replicated to nearly equivalent titers as H1N1pdm09. All H5N1 viruses demonstrated similar cell tropism in cells from the upper and lower respiratory tract, infecting more ciliated than non-ciliated cells relative to H1N1pdm09. H1N1, H5N1 B3.13 D1.1 infection induced similar innate immune factors, with nasal epithelial cells producing higher levels compared to bronchial epithelial cells. These data suggest that genotype B3.13 and D1.1 H5N1 viruses show different temperature dependent replication patterns compared to H1N1pdm09.

elements_en.methods: The researchers assessed replication by measuring plaque sizes on MDCK cells at different temperatures (33°C, 37°C, and 39°C) and evaluated infectious virus production in differentiated human nasal and bronchial epithelial cultures.
elements_en.main_results: All H5N1 viruses showed increased plaque sizes on MDCK cells at 37°C and 39°C compared to H1N1pdm09. In human respiratory epithelial cultures, H5N1 B3.13 replicated to nearly equivalent titers as H1N1pdm09 at 33°C, while H5N1 D1.1 showed restricted replication at 37°C and 39°C.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 exhibit distinct temperature-dependent replication patterns compared to H1N1pdm09, which may have implications for their potential to infect and transmit among mammalian hosts.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the replication behavior of H5N1 viruses in human respiratory tissues, which could inform surveillance and risk assessment strategies for potential zoonotic transmission.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro cell cultures and does not account for in vivo factors, which may affect replication dynamics. The evidence is moderate due to the controlled experimental setting.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在研究 H5N1 基因型 B3.13 和 D1.1 在人类呼吸道上皮细胞培养物中的复制特征,解决有关它们在哺乳动物物种之间感染和传播的潜力的知识差距。

elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过测量不同温度(33°C、37°C​​ 和 39°C)下 MDCK 细胞上的噬斑大小来评估复制,并评估分化的人鼻和支气管上皮培养物中感染性病毒的产生。
elements_zh.main_results: 与 H1N1pdm09 相比,所有 H5N1 病毒在 37°C 和 39°C 的 MDCK 细胞上显示出噬斑大小增加。在人呼吸道上皮培养物中,H5N1 B3.13 在 33°C 时复制到几乎与 H1N1pdm09 相同的滴度,而 H5N1 D1.1 在 37°C 和 39°C 时表现出有限的复制。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,与 H1N1pdm09 相比,H5N1 基因型 B3.13 和 D1.1 表现出明显的温度依赖性复制模式,这可能对其在哺乳动物 宿主 中感染和传播的潜力产生影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果提供了对 H5N1 病毒在人类呼吸道组织中的复制行为的深入了解,这可以为 监测 和潜在人畜共患 传播 的风险评估策略提供信息。

papers.title_zh: 甲型流感病毒 H5N1 基因型 B3.13 和 D1.1 在源自上呼吸道和下呼吸道的原代人呼吸道上皮细胞培养物中表现出温度依赖性复制限制。
papers.source_body_en: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b avian influenza A viruses pose a significant threat to wild animal populations, domesticated animals, and potentially, the human population. For H5N1s to infect and transmit among mammalian species, mutations for improved utilization of mammalian receptors and enhanced replication at the lower temperatures of the upper respiratory tract need to be acquired. A human H1N1pdm09-like virus was compared to H5N1 genotypes B3.13 and D1.1 for replication at 33{o}C, 37{o}C, and 39{o}C - temperatures consistent with the upper and lower respiratory tract in humans, and dairy cow udder tissue. All H5N1 viruses had increased plaque sizes on MDCK cells at 37{o}C and 39{o}C compared to H1N1pdm09. In primary, differentiated human nasal and bronchial epithelial cultures, all H5N1 viruses show restricted infectious virus production compared to H1N1 at 33{o}C. While H5N1 D1.1 also showed restricted replication at 37{o}C and 39{o}C, the H5N1 B3.13 replicated to nearly equivalent titers as H1N1pdm09. All H5N1 viruses demonstrated similar cell tropism in cells from the upper and lower respiratory tract, infecting more ciliated than non-ciliated cells relative to H1N1pdm09. H1N1, H5N1 B3.13 D1.1 infection induced similar innate immune factors, with nasal epithelial cells producing higher levels compared to bronchial epithelial cells. These data suggest that genotype B3.13 and D1.1 H5N1 viruses show different temperature dependent replication patterns compared to H1N1pdm09.
papers.abstract_zh: H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 甲型禽流感病毒对野生动物种群、家养动物以及潜在的人类种群构成重大威胁。为了使 H5N1 在哺乳动物物种之间感染和传播,需要获得 突变 来提高哺乳动物受体的利用率并增强上呼吸道较低温度下的复制。将人类 H1N1pdm09 样病毒与 H5N1 基因型 B3.13 和 D1.1 进行比较,以在 33°C、37°C 和 39°C 下复制,这些温度与人类上呼吸道和下呼吸道以及奶牛乳房组织一致。与 H1N1pdm09 相比,所有 H5N1 病毒在 37{o}C 和 39{o}C 下 MDCK 细胞上的噬斑大小均有所增加。在原代、分化的人类鼻腔和支气管上皮培养物中,与 H1N1 相比,所有 H5N1 病毒在 33°C 下的感染性病毒产量均受到限制。虽然 H5N1 D1.1 在 37{o}C 和 39{o}C 下也表现出有限的复制,但 H5N1 B3.13 的复制滴度几乎与 H1N1pdm09 相同。所有 H5N1 病毒在上呼吸道和下呼吸道细胞中都表现出相似的细胞趋向性,相对于 H1N1pdm09,它们感染的纤毛细胞多于非纤毛细胞。H1N1、H5N1 B3.13 D1.1 感染诱导类似的先天免疫因子,鼻上皮细胞产生的水平高于支气管上皮细胞。这些数据表明,与 H1N1pdm09 相比,基因型 B3.13 和 D1.1 H5N1 病毒表现出不同的温度依赖性复制模式。

papers.title: An LLM enabled real-time estimation of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness from social media data
papers.abstract: Influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) is estimated from a limited number of clinics using a test-negative design. These standard estimates face geographic, temporal, and operational constraints. Using Twitter/X data, we applied few-shot chain-of-thought prompting to identify self-reported vaccination status and influenza test results, then implemented a test-negative-like design to estimate VE. Our estimates fell within the range of interim reports and could complement current systems, improving feasibility, timeliness, and scalability.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of social media data to estimate seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) through an LLM-based approach. Traditional VE estimation methods are constrained by geographic, temporal, and operational limitations, prompting the need for alternative strategies. By analyzing self-reported vaccination status and influenza test results from Twitter/X, the researchers implemented a test-negative-like design to estimate VE. Their results aligned with interim reports, suggesting that this method could complement existing systems and improve the feasibility, timeliness, and scalability of VE estimation. The study highlights the potential of integrating social media data into public health surveillance but acknowledges limitations such as potential biases and limited generalizability. The evidence is considered strong due to the consistency of findings with established reports.

papers.title: Significant upregulation of GSDMD and TfR-1 genes following A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B infections
papers.abstract: Influenza viruses, as important respiratory viruses for seasonal flu, are responsible for yearly mortality among human populations. Among different and complex interactions within the cell, pyroptosis and ferroptosis have emerged as two main cell death pathways that are correlated to inflammation following influenza infection. In this study, we have investigated GSDMD (pyroptosis marker) and TfR-1 (ferroptosis marker) mRNA expression, 48 h post-infection (hpi) in A549 infected cells with different types of influenza viruses. A549 cells were infected with A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B with 100 TCID50. RNA was extracted by RNJIA RNA extraction kit (RNJIA, ROJE, Iran) 48 hpi, and mRNA expression of GSDMD and TfR-1 was assessed by SYBR Green qRT-PCR. Gene expression data were analyzed using both non-parametric and parametric statistical tests, followed by pairwise post-hoc comparisons. The consistent upregulation of GSDMD and TfR-1 across A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B compared to the control groups suggests the involvement of these pro-pyroptotic and pro-ferroptotic factors associated to pyrotposis and ferroptosis cell death pathways following inflammation, 48 hpi. While GSDMD had sharpest upregulation in A/H1N1 compared to A/H3N2 and Flu-B, TfR-1 upregulation showed different pattern with highest upregulation in A/H3N2. In total, our study supports the potential involvement of GSDMD and TfR-1 which are associated with pyroptosis and ferroptosis that are active following different types of influenza viruses.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that GSDMD and TfR-1 are involved in pyroptosis and ferroptosis pathways following inflammation caused by different influenza viruses. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may inform future research on the role of pyroptosis and ferroptosis in influenza-induced inflammation, potentially aiding in the development of targeted therapies or diagnostic tools for seasonal influenza.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the upregulation of GSDMD and TfR-1 genes in A549 cells following infection with A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and Flu-B viruses. The findings suggest that these molecular mechanisms may play a role in the pathogenesis of seasonal influenza. While the study provides novel insights into gene expression changes, its in vitro design limits the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on gene expression analysis without clinical outcomes. The results may inform future research on the molecular basis of influenza-induced inflammation and its implications for therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_zh: 流感病毒作为季节性流感的重要呼吸道病毒,是导致人群每年出现死亡率的原因。在细胞内不同且复杂的相互作用中,细胞焦亡和铁死亡已成为与流感感染后炎症相关的两种主要细胞死亡途径。在这项研究中,我们研究了感染不同类型流感病毒的 A549 感染细胞中 48 小时感染后 (hpi) 的 GSDMD(细胞焦亡标记)和 TfR-1(铁死亡标记)mRNA 表达。A549 细胞用 100 TCID50 感染 A/H1N1、A/H3N2 和 Flu-B。使用RNJIA RNA提取试剂盒(RNJIA,ROJE,伊朗)提取48 hpi的RNA,并通过SYBR Green qRT-PCR评估GSDMD和TfR-1的mRNA表达。使用非参数和参数统计检验分析基因表达数据,然后进行成对事后比较。与对照组相比,GSDMD 和 TfR-1 在 A/H1N1、A/H3N2 和 Flu-B 中持续上调,表明这些促焦亡和促铁死亡因子与炎症后 48 hpi 后的细胞焦亡和铁死亡途径相关。与 A/H3N2 和 Flu-B 相比,GSDMD 在 A/H1N1 中上调最明显,但 TfR-1 上调表现出不同的模式,在 A/H3N2 中上调最高。总的来说,我们的研究支持 GSDMD 和 TfR-1 的潜在参与,它们与不同类型流感病毒后活跃的细胞焦亡和铁死亡相关。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,GSDMD 和 TfR-1 参与不同流感病毒引起的炎症后的细胞焦亡和铁死亡途径。这项研究为与 季节性流感 相关的细胞死亡分子机制提供了新的见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能为未来关于细胞焦亡和铁死亡在流感引起的炎症中的作用的研究提供信息,可能有助于开发 季节性流感 的靶向疗法或诊断工具。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于使用 A549 细胞进行体外分析,可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答。证据是中等的,因为它基于基因表达分析,没有直接的临床结果。

PEARLS Equine influenza virus at 70: What horses taught us about flu Laura Mojsiejczuk1, Thomas M. Chambers2, Pablo R. Murcia 1* 1 MRC-University of Glasgow Centre for Virus Research, Institute of Infection, Immunity and Inflammation, College of Medical, Veterinary and Life Sciences, University of Glasgow, Glasgow, Scotland, United Kingdom, 2 Department of Veterinary Science, Maxwell H. Gluck Equine Research Center, University of Kentucky, Lexington, Kentucky, United States of America * Pablo.Murcia@glasgow.ac.uk This year marks the 70th anniversary of the first documented isolation of equine influenza virus (EIV). In May 1956, major outbreaks of respiratory disease in horses took place in the former Republic of Czechoslovakia. The presence of antibodies against influenza A in serum from affected horses, together with observed similarities in clinical course with influenza in humans, led Sovinova and colleagues to “inves­ tigate the problem in greater detail”. Most nasal washes cultured in embryonated chicken eggs failed due to contamination, but sample 262 remained sterile, yielding A/equine/Prague/56 (H7N7) [1], marking the start of EIV research and initiating a new area of influenza research. While poultry and swine are also kept in dispersed, inter­ connected populations, horses uniquely combine those characteristics with a long lifespan and global mobility (trailing only humans as the most common commercial air travellers, for breeding and performance purposes), an intersection of epidemio­ logical features that more closely resembles that of humans and makes EIV a partic­ ularly informative model system. This Pearl article is our personal view that aims to highlight how studies on EIV have informed fundamental concepts of influenza virus biology, evolution, and epidemiology (Fig 1). Horses played a role in the history of human influenza Influenza A viruses (IAVs) exhibit a complex ecology rooted in their natural avian reservoir, from which multiple cross-species transmission events have led to docu­ mented spillover and host shifts from birds to mammals and also among mammalian species. Major human pandemics have arisen from such processes. Within this context, horses have historically been considered as potential sources of zoonotic infections. Influenza has been recognised as a disease of the horse since 1299 AD. Before the invention and widespread use of the automobile, contact rates between people and horses were much higher because horses were the main means of trans­ port. While empirical evidence is lacking, it has been suggested that horses played a role in the genesis of epidemic influenza [2] because human influenza epidemics were usually preceded by equine influenza outbreaks (importantly, this pattern dis­ appeared as horses were replaced by cars). Indeed, a recently published hypothesis PLOS Pathogens | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551 August 28, 2026 2 / 6 posed that horses may have contributed to the genesis of the virus that caused the 1918 pandemic [3], challenging conventional accounts. A second EIV subtype -this time an H3N8 virus- emerged in 1963 [4]. In 1965, Minuse and colleagues reported serological evidence of cross-reactive anti-H3 antibodies in individuals born between 1874 and 1891, predating the emergence of H3 IAVs in humans and pigs [5]. These findings supported the idea, already under discussion at the time, that influenza virus subtypes may “recycle” and that animal reservoirs could play a role in this process. EIV revealed the hidden diversity within individual hosts H3N8 EIV was used as a model system in pioneering studies aiming to elucidate the patterns of influenza within-host diversity and evolution. For decades, RNA viruses had been recognised as mixtures of genetic variants whose frequencies change rap­ idly during infection [6]. At a time when next-generation sequencing was in its infancy, clonal sequencing was combined with in vivo experiments in horses to measure for the first time the intra-host diversity of a mammalian IAV in its natural host. By iden­ tifying and counting mutations in the haemagglutinin gene of infected horses, those studies showed that acute equine influenza infections generate genetically distinct viral subpopulations beyond the consensus sequence and that most naturally arising mutations are deleterious [7]. It was also observed that some minority variants can persist for multiple days and even be transmitted, suggesting that virus transmission bottlenecks were not as narrow as previously perceived. These findings were later confirmed in natural outbreaks [8], also using clonal sequencing. EIV intra-host data contributed empirical evidence for the development of a within-host evolutionary model that, applied to H5N1 in the ferret transmission model, showed that respiratory droplet-transmissible variants can arise during a single mammalian infection, yet remain below consensus detection thresholds, and that the proportion reached by these variants determines the likelihood of onward transmis­ sion [9]. Since those early EIV studies based on the analyses of only a few thousand haemagglutinin sequences, advances in sequencing technologies (currently reaching millions of sequencing reads covering the entire genome) and bioinformatic pipelines have refined this picture, confirming that most within-host variants are short-lived, with strong purifying selection and genetic drift dominating evolutionary dynamics during acute infection. Furthermore, empirical estimates in large human cohorts suggest relatively tight transmission bottlenecks and limited evidence for sustained positive selection of antigenic variants during acute infection [10]. Comparative anal­ yses across viral models (e.g., dengue virus and cytomegalovirus) suggest that such constraints are not unique to influenza [6]. EIV linked epidemic patterns to the long-term evolution of influenza A viruses Phylodynamics is a conceptual framework formalised by Grenfell and colleagues that integrates immunodynamics, epidemiology and evolutionary biology to explain how within-host processes and population-level epidemic dynamics jointly shape viral Competing interests: The authors have declared that no competing interests exist. PLOS Pathogens | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551 August 28, 2026 3 / 6 phylogenies [11]. This theoretical framework has massively increased our understanding of infectious disease dynamics. As noted by Bryan Grenfell during the Commemorative lecture of the 2022 Kyoto Prize in Basic Science, the study of epidemics of influenza in horses stimulated ideas that became central to the theories in phylodynamics [12]. Data from experimental infections in horses were used to parameterise viral shedding and immune responses, enabling quantifica­ tion of the impact of viral fitness in the context of host immune status and determination of transmission probability [11]. EIV has also informed our understanding of long-term IAV evolution. Worobey et al. reconstructed the evolutionary history of IAV across multiple hosts and identified a synchronised global sweep of the internal genes of avian influenza viruses in the nineteenth century [13]. Notably, their analyses placed equine H7N7 as a basal sister lineage to avian, human, swine, and equine H3N8 clades. Interestingly, the branch that separates those sister lineages covers the 1866– 1878 period, which includes the major equine influenza epizootic of 1872 and leads Worobey and colleagues to speculate that “some epidemiological event” associated with that epizootic might have precipitated the global sweep of internal IAV genes. However, this proposal remains controversial: the back-extrapolation of any causal role for EIV or H7N7 in the broader emergence of mammalian and human influenza lacks direct empirical support. Timeline showing EIV-specific research milestones (upper track) and corresponding contributions to broader influenza and virology concepts (lower track) from 1956 to the present, which have shaped modern understanding of influenza across multiple host species. Icons adapted from Pixabay, PhyloPic.org, and Wikimedia Commons. Abbreviations: EIV, equine influenza virus; IAV, influenza A virus; R, effective reproduction number. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551.g001 PLOS Pathogens | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1014551 August 28, 2026 4 / 6 EIV documented decades of viral evolution in real time EIV offers a remarkably complete, real-time record of influenza virus macroevolution in a nonhuman mammal, from a putative avian spillover in 1963 that led to the emergence of H3N8 EIV (and subsequent replacement of the H7N7 sub­ type), through decades of enzootic diversification and competitive lineage turnover, and including a second host jump into dogs [14]. Canine influenza virus (CIV) was first reported in racing greyhounds in 2004. Unusually among mammalian influenza viruses, it emerged through the direct mammal-to-mammal transfer of an entire nonreassortant equine virus that then adapted to and circulated enzootically in dogs; it remains the first documented interspecies transfer with the donor species unequivocally identified by whole-genome sequencing. Sustained mainly by dense, interconnected shelter and kennel dog populations, H3N8 CIV never spread beyond North America, was last detected in 2016, and is presumed to be extinct [15]. Phylogenetic analyses of global H3N8 EIV complete genomes showed that distinct clades can co-circulate for extended periods, and that intra-subtype reassortment is relatively frequent, in addition to typical diversification driven by gradual substitutions on a single lineage observed in human IAVs. Notably, H3N8 EIV evolved at a slower rate than other mamma­ lian IAVs, potentially due to a weaker immune selection in its host population [16]. EIV taught us practical lessons about influenza control and eradication EIV research has also contributed to our general understanding of influenza epidemiology. Vaccine studies by the late Jennifer Mumford at the Animal Health Trust in Newmarket, United Kingdom, provided important information regard­ ing vaccine composition (in terms of viral strains to be included as well as adjuvants) and duration of vaccine-mediated immunity, which in turn informed vaccination schedules. While this research contributed significantly to the development of measures to control equine influenza, data generated by those highly controlled experimental infections informed epidemi­ ological models that explicitly measured, for the first time, how amino acid differences between immunising and circulating influenza strains impact on the effective reproductive number R, and as a result on epidemic size [17]. Beyond controlled experiments, population-level genomic analyses revealed that EIV displayed a significant drop in global genetic diversity after vaccination became mandatory in competition horses in the early 1980s, providing a field- scale example of interventions causing measurable population bottlenecks [16]. In Australia, a large EIV outbreak in 2007 affected more than 70,000 horses, but the virus was later eradicated by a combination of zoning, movement restrictions, vaccination (using DIVA vaccines, see below) and increased biosecurity [18]. To the best of our knowledge, this remains the only documented case of active eradication of a mammalian IAV following widespread introduction into a country. A recent study suggests that EIV could be eradicated from the United Kingdom, as continuous endemic transmission might not be supported [19]. As with human IAVs, vaccination is the best prophylactic measure recommended- and sometimes required- for horses at risk of exposure, such as by travel to competitions. Several EIV vaccine platforms are available, including inactivated virus, ISCOM-based, modified-live virus, and recombinant canarypox-vectored vaccines, and plant-based virus-like particles expressing HA, which offer a potentially viable alternative, as they are easier to update and produce [20]. The recombinant canarypox-vectored vaccines enable differentiation of infected from vaccinated animals (DIVA), a capability that was essential during the 2007 epizootic eradication campaign in Australia. EIV undergoes antigenic drift, though at a slower rate than human IAVs. Furthermore, vaccine strains are updated less frequently than those for human seasonal influenza, likely due to limited virological and economic incentives associated with the relatively small veterinary market. Conclusion In sum, the study of EIV has made a significant contribution to our current understanding of influenza virus infections not only in horses but also in other mammalian hosts (including humans), illustrating the importance of comparative approaches in virology research. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study explores how research on equine influenza virus (EIV) has contributed to understanding fundamental aspects of influenza virus biology, evolution, and epidemiology, particularly in relation to human seasonal influenza viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a narrative review of historical and contemporary research on equine influenza virus, focusing on its role as a model system for understanding influenza dynamics. It includes data from outbreaks in horses and comparisons with human influenza.
analysis.methods: The authors conducted a comprehensive review of literature and historical records related to equine influenza virus, analyzing its epidemiological features, genetic evolution, and interactions with host populations. analysis.main_results: The study highlights that equine influenza virus has provided critical insights into influenza virus ecology, evolution, and host interactions, particularly due to its unique epidemiological characteristics resembling those of human seasonal influenza viruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that EIV has been a valuable model for studying influenza, offering a unique perspective on viral transmission and evolution. This is a novel contribution to understanding how animal models can inform human influenza research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that studying equine influenza virus can enhance our understanding of human seasonal influenza, aiding in the development of more effective surveillance, diagnosis, and control strategies for human influenza.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the historical and scientific contributions of equine influenza virus (EIV) to understanding influenza virus biology, evolution, and epidemiology. It highlights how EIV, with its unique characteristics such as global mobility and long lifespan, serves as an informative model for human seasonal influenza. The authors review key findings from EIV research, emphasizing its role in elucidating cross-species transmission and host interactions. They argue that insights from EIV studies have informed fundamental concepts in influenza research, offering a novel perspective on the virus's behavior. The study underscores the importance of animal models in understanding human influenza, with implications for surveillance and control strategies. However, the reliance on historical data and observational studies limits the strength of the evidence, though the analysis remains grounded in well-documented findings.

papers.title: Site-specific microRNA responses in lungs of pigs depend on the host-adaptation of H1N1 influenza A virus
papers.abstract: Cross-species transmission of influenza A virus (IAV) represents a major risk for emergence of new pandemics, however, the host molecular responses invoked by cross-species IAV infection remain incompletely defined. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are important post-transcriptional regulators of innate immunity, but their role during infection with IAV strains of the same subtype but of different host origin has not been investigated. Here, we investigated pulmonary miRNA responses in upper and lower lung sites from pigs inoculated with either a swine-adapted (swH1N1) or a human-adapted (huH1N1) IAV originating from the 2009H1N1 pandemic strain. High-throughput microfluidic RT-qPCR profiling of 115 miRNAs and selected antiviral genes revealed strain-dependent differences, with 33 miRNAs being differentially expressed in pig lungs (upper and lower lung) after human-adapted IAV infection, while only eight miRNAs were altered after swine-adapted IAV infection. Expression of several miRNAs correlated inversely with predicted target pattern recognition receptor (PRR) and interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) transcripts after huH1N1 infection, including miR-19a/b, miR-21-5p, and miR-93-3p, suggesting miRNA-mediated fine-tuning of antiviral signaling. Notably, extensive downregulation of miRNAs in the lower lungs after huH1N1 infection coincided with robust ISG induction, despite huH1N1 viral lung load being comparable to swH1N1 viral load. The swine-adapted IAV, in contrast, triggered stronger RIG-I-like receptor and cGAS transcription without substantial miRNA changes. Together, these findings demonstrate that pulmonary miRNA responses to IAV are both strain- and lung site-specific and may contribute to shaping the outcome of infection depending on the degree of viral host adaptation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the host molecular responses to influenza A virus (IAV) in pigs, focusing on the differences in pulmonary miRNA expression between human-adapted (huH1N1) and swine-adapted (swH1N1) IAV strains. The research highlights that miRNA responses are strain- and lung site-specific, with huH1N1 infection leading to significant miRNA downregulation and ISG induction, while swH1N1 infection triggered stronger RIG-I-like receptor and cGAS transcription without substantial miRNA changes. These findings suggest that miRNA-mediated antiviral signaling may play a role in shaping the outcome of IAV infection depending on the degree of host adaptation. The study contributes to understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying cross-species IAV transmission and may inform future research on viral host adaptation and immune responses.

papers.title_zh: 猪肺部的位点特异性 microRNA 反应取决于 H1N1 甲型流感病毒的 宿主 适应
papers.source_body_en: Cross-species transmission of influenza A virus (IAV) represents a major risk for emergence of new pandemics, however, the host molecular responses invoked by cross-species IAV infection remain incompletely defined. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are important post-transcriptional regulators of innate immunity, but their role during infection with IAV strains of the same subtype but of different host origin has not been investigated. Here, we investigated pulmonary miRNA responses in upper and lower lung sites from pigs inoculated with either a swine-adapted (swH1N1) or a human-adapted (huH1N1) IAV originating from the 2009H1N1 pandemic strain. High-throughput microfluidic RT-qPCR profiling of 115 miRNAs and selected antiviral genes revealed strain-dependent differences, with 33 miRNAs being differentially expressed in pig lungs (upper and lower lung) after human-adapted IAV infection, while only eight miRNAs were altered after swine-adapted IAV infection. Expression of several miRNAs correlated inversely with predicted target pattern recognition receptor (PRR) and interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) transcripts after huH1N1 infection, including miR-19a/b, miR-21-5p, and miR-93-3p, suggesting miRNA-mediated fine-tuning of antiviral signaling. Notably, extensive downregulation of miRNAs in the lower lungs after huH1N1 infection coincided with robust ISG induction, despite huH1N1 viral lung load being comparable to swH1N1 viral load. The swine-adapted IAV, in contrast, triggered stronger RIG-I-like receptor and cGAS transcription without substantial miRNA changes. Together, these findings demonstrate that pulmonary miRNA responses to IAV are both strain- and lung site-specific and may contribute to shaping the outcome of infection depending on the degree of viral host adaptation.

papers.title: Neuraminidase and secretory pathway stress converge to remodel host glycosylation during influenza A virus infection
papers.abstract: Abstract Glycosylation is critical for viral-host cell interactions in influenza A virus (IAV) infection, but we lack a comprehensive understanding of how IAV infection shapes the host glycoproteome. Here, we performed liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic characterisation of the dynamic subcellular responses to an in vitro time course infection of human A549 cells. IAV infection resulted in only modest changes to the subcellular proteome, but robust and significant changes to the host secreted and organelle glycome and glycoproteome. Infection caused reductions in sialylation across the N- and O-glyco(proteo)me; increased oligomannose, paucimannose, and phosphorylated glycans; and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. Desialylation was greater when glycans were fucosylated; for sialic acid linked α2,3 or on the α3 arm; on larger, complex glycans; and on proteins likely to be more accessible to IAV neuraminidase (NA). Subtle activation of the unfolded protein response in infection was associated with a doubling of oligomannose N-glycosylation. Glycans were shorter in infection, implicating IAV-induced disruption of Golgi glycoprotein flux as a mechanism that reduces host glycoprotein sialylation and promotes virion release, independent of NA activity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how influenza A virus (IAV) infection alters the host glycoproteome, as glycosylation is essential for viral-host interactions but the mechanisms remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used an in vitro time course infection model of human A549 cells, employing liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to characterise proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic changes during IAV infection.
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted LC-MS/MS proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic analyses to examine the dynamic subcellular responses to IAV infection, focusing on changes in glycan structures and their association with host cell processes.
analysis.main_results: IAV infection led to reductions in sialylation across N- and O-glyco(proteo)me, increases in oligomannose, paucimannose, and phosphorylated glycans, and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. Subtle activation of the unfolded protein response was linked to a doubling of oligomannose N-glycosylation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that IAV-induced disruption of Golgi glycoprotein flux reduces host glycoprotein sialylation and facilitates virion release, independent of neuraminidase activity, offering a novel mechanism for viral replication.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms of IAV infection, which could inform the development of targeted therapies and improve understanding of host-virus interactions in seasonal influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro models, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions, and the evidence is based on proteomic and glycomic analyses without direct functional validation, resulting in moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how influenza A virus (IAV) infection alters host glycosylation patterns, revealing significant changes in the secreted and organelle glycome and glycoproteome. Using an in vitro time course infection model of human A549 cells, the researchers observed reductions in sialylation, increases in specific glycans, and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. They also noted a subtle activation of the unfolded protein response associated with increased oligomannose N-glycosylation. The findings suggest that IAV-induced disruption of Golgi glycoprotein flux reduces host glycoprotein sialylation and promotes virion release, independent of neuraminidase activity. These results offer a novel mechanism for IAV replication and could inform future therapeutic strategies. However, the study's reliance on in vitro models and lack of direct functional validation limit the confidence in its conclusions, resulting in a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探究甲型流感病毒(IAV)感染如何改变宿主糖蛋白组,因糖基化对病毒-宿主相互作用至关重要,但其机制仍不甚明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用人类 A549 细胞的体外时程感染模型,采用液相色谱-串联质谱 (LC-MS/MS) 来表征 IAV 感染期间的蛋白质组、糖组和糖蛋白质组变化。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员进行了 LC-MS/MS 蛋白质组、糖组和糖蛋白质组分析,以检查 IAV 感染的动态亚细胞反应,重点关注聚糖结构的变化及其与 宿主 细胞过程的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: IAV 感染导致 N- 和 O- 糖(蛋白质)组唾液酸化减少,寡甘露糖、寡甘露糖和磷酸化聚糖以及较短的杂合/复合聚糖增加。未折叠蛋白反应的微妙激活与寡甘露糖 N-糖基化的加倍有关。

analysis_en.methods: The researchers conducted LC-MS/MS proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic analyses to examine the dynamic subcellular responses to IAV infection, focusing on changes in glycan structures and their association with host cell processes.
analysis_en.main_results: IAV infection led to reductions in sialylation across N- and O-glyco(proteo)me, increases in oligomannose, paucimannose, and phosphorylated glycans, and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that IAV-induced disruption of Golgi glycoprotein flux reduces host glycoprotein sialylation and facilitates virion release, independent of neuraminidase activity, offering a novel mechanism for viral replication.

papers.title_zh: 甲型流感病毒感染期间神经氨酸酶和分泌途径应激汇聚重塑 宿主 糖基化
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Glycosylation is critical for viral-host cell interactions in influenza A virus (IAV) infection, but we lack a comprehensive understanding of how IAV infection shapes the host glycoproteome. Here, we performed liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) proteomic, glycomic, and glycoproteomic characterisation of the dynamic subcellular responses to an in vitro time course infection of human A549 cells. IAV infection resulted in only modest changes to the subcellular proteome, but robust and significant changes to the host secreted and organelle glycome and glycoproteome. Infection caused reductions in sialylation across the N- and O-glyco(proteo)me; increased oligomannose, paucimannose, and phosphorylated glycans; and shorter hybrid/complex glycans. Desialylation was greater when glycans were fucosylated; for sialic acid linked α2,3 or on the α3 arm; on larger, complex glycans; and on proteins likely to be more accessible to IAV neuraminidase (NA). Subtle activation of the unfolded protein response in infection was associated with a doubling of oligomannose N-glycosylation. Glycans were shorter in infection, implicating IAV-induced disruption of Golgi glycoprotein flux as a mechanism that reduces host glycoprotein sialylation and promotes virion release, independent of NA activity.

papers.title: Pre-existing systemic and nasal antibodies against avian H5 influenza A viruses vary according to childhood imprinting
papers.abstract: Avian influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a constant pandemic threat, with the recent 2.3.4.4b clade of the H5 subtype causing high pathogenicity and spreading across animal species and geographic locations. Understanding human pre-existing immunity to avian H5 IAV can inform on population susceptibility, a critical aspect of pandemic preparedness. To that end, we analyzed the IAV HA-specific antibodies across individuals born between 1928 and 1999 with different early life exposures to IAV subtypes. Individuals born prior to 1957 had the highest pre-existing serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including the 2.3.4.4b H5 and a group 1 HA stem antigen. These birth year-specific patterns were not reflected in the limited pre-existing serum neutralizing antibodies detectable against a 2.3.4.4b H5 IAV or in H5-specific memory B cell populations. They were, however, evident in pre-existing nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5, which were greater in individuals born prior to 1957. Our findings demonstrate that the immunological biases afforded by early life exposure extend to antibodies detected in the nasal mucosa, the site of IAV replication.IMPORTANCEUnderstating pre-existing immunity to influenza A viruses (IAVs) of pandemic potential is an important aspect of pandemic preparedness. This includes an understanding of the heterogeneity of pre-existing immunity across the population. Here, we demonstrate that pre-existing antibodies to H5 IAV vary according to the year of birth and childhood imprinting. We demonstrate that this is the case for both systemic and nasal antibodies, highlighting the importance of understanding pre-existing mucosal immunity at the sites of influenza virus replication.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Avian influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a pandemic threat, and understanding human pre-existing immunity to avian H5 IAV is critical for pandemic preparedness. The study aimed to determine whether pre-existing antibodies to H5 IAV vary according to childhood imprinting and early life exposure to IAV subtypes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed IAV HA-specific antibodies in individuals born between 1928 and 1999, stratified by birth year to reflect different early life exposures to IAV subtypes. Participants were selected to examine systemic and nasal antibody responses to H5 IAV.
analysis.methods: Serum and nasal samples were analyzed for HA-specific antibodies, including serum neutralizing antibodies, memory B cell populations, and nasal IgG and IgA titers against H5 IAV. Antibody levels were measured to assess pre-existing immunity.
analysis.main_results: Individuals born prior to 1957 exhibited the highest pre-existing serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including H5 and a group 1 HA stem antigen. However, these birth year-specific patterns were not reflected in serum neutralizing antibodies against H5 IAV or H5-specific memory B cell populations. Pre-existing nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5 were greater in individuals born prior to 1957.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that immunological biases from early life exposure extend to antibodies detected in the nasal mucosa, the primary site of IAV replication. This highlights the importance of understanding mucosal immunity in pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests that childhood imprinting influences pre-existing mucosal immunity to H5 IAV, which may inform surveillance strategies and vaccine design targeting pandemic threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on pre-existing antibodies and does not address functional immunity or protection against infection. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on cross-sectional sampling and does not establish causality.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined pre-existing antibodies to avian H5 influenza A virus (IAV) in humans, stratified by birth year to reflect early life exposure to IAV subtypes. Individuals born before 1957 showed higher serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including H5, but this pattern did not extend to serum neutralizing antibodies or H5-specific memory B cells. Notably, nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5 were elevated in this group, indicating that childhood imprinting influences mucosal immunity at the site of IAV replication. The findings underscore the importance of understanding mucosal antibody responses for pandemic preparedness, particularly for avian H5 IAV. However, the study is limited by its cross-sectional design and lack of functional immunity assessment, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型禽流感病毒 (IAV) 构成大流行威胁,了解人类对禽 H5 IAV 已有的免疫力对于预防大流行至关重要。该研究旨在确定预先存在的 H5 IAV 抗体是否会根据童年印记和早年接触 IAV 亚型而变化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 1928 年至 1999 年间出生的个体的 IAV HA 特异性抗体,并按出生年份分层,以反映不同的早期 IAV 亚型暴露情况。选择参与者来检查对 H5 IAV 的全身和鼻腔抗体反应。
elements_zh.methods: 分析血清和鼻腔样本中的 HA 特异性抗体,包括血清中和抗体、记忆 B 细胞群以及针对 H5 IAV 的鼻腔 IgG 和 IgA 滴度。测量抗体水平以评估预先存在的免疫力。
elements_zh.main_results: 1957 年之前出生的个体表现出针对第 1 组 HA 抗原(包括 H5 和第 1 组 HA 干抗原)的最高现有血清抗体。然而,这些出生年份特异性模式并未反映在针对 H5 IAV 或 H5 特异性记忆 B 细胞群的血清中和抗体中。1957 年之前出生的个体中预先存在的 H5 鼻腔 IgG 和 IgA 滴度更高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,生命早期接触造成的免疫偏差延伸到鼻粘膜(IAV 复制的主要部位)中检测到的抗体。这凸显了了解粘膜免疫在大流行防范中的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究表明,童年印记影响预先存在的对 H5 IAV 的粘膜免疫,这可能为针对大流行威胁的 监测 策略和 疫苗 设计提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其关注的是预先存在的抗体,并且没有涉及功能性免疫或针对感染的保护。证据是中等的,因为它依赖于横截面抽样并且没有建立因果关系。

analysis_en.methods: Serum and nasal samples were analyzed for HA-specific antibodies, including serum neutralizing antibodies, memory B cell populations, and nasal IgG and IgA titers against H5 IAV. Antibody levels were measured to assess pre-existing immunity.
analysis_en.main_results: Individuals born prior to 1957 exhibited the highest pre-existing serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including H5 and a group 1 HA stem antigen. However, these birth year-specific patterns were not reflected in serum neutralizing antibodies against H5 IAV or H5-specific memory B cell populations. Pre-existing nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5 were greater in individuals born prior to 1957.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that immunological biases from early life exposure extend to antibodies detected in the nasal mucosa, the primary site of IAV replication. This highlights the importance of understanding mucosal immunity in pandemic preparedness.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests that childhood imprinting influences pre-existing mucosal immunity to H5 IAV, which may inform surveillance strategies and vaccine design targeting pandemic threats.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on pre-existing antibodies and does not address functional immunity or protection against infection. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on cross-sectional sampling and does not establish causality.

papers.source_body_en: Avian influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a constant pandemic threat, with the recent 2.3.4.4b clade of the H5 subtype causing high pathogenicity and spreading across animal species and geographic locations. Understanding human pre-existing immunity to avian H5 IAV can inform on population susceptibility, a critical aspect of pandemic preparedness. To that end, we analyzed the IAV HA-specific antibodies across individuals born between 1928 and 1999 with different early life exposures to IAV subtypes. Individuals born prior to 1957 had the highest pre-existing serum antibodies to group 1 HA antigens, including the 2.3.4.4b H5 and a group 1 HA stem antigen. These birth year-specific patterns were not reflected in the limited pre-existing serum neutralizing antibodies detectable against a 2.3.4.4b H5 IAV or in H5-specific memory B cell populations. They were, however, evident in pre-existing nasal IgG and IgA titers to H5, which were greater in individuals born prior to 1957. Our findings demonstrate that the immunological biases afforded by early life exposure extend to antibodies detected in the nasal mucosa, the site of IAV replication.IMPORTANCEUnderstating pre-existing immunity to influenza A viruses (IAVs) of pandemic potential is an important aspect of pandemic preparedness. This includes an understanding of the heterogeneity of pre-existing immunity across the population. Here, we demonstrate that pre-existing antibodies to H5 IAV vary according to the year of birth and childhood imprinting. We demonstrate that this is the case for both systemic and nasal antibodies, highlighting the importance of understanding pre-existing mucosal immunity at the sites of influenza virus replication.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型禽流感病毒 (IAV) 构成大流行威胁,了解人类对禽 H5 IAV 已有的免疫力对于预防大流行至关重要。该研究旨在确定预先存在的 H5 IAV 抗体是否会根据童年印记和早年接触 IAV 亚型而变化。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 1928 年至 1999 年间出生的个体的 IAV HA 特异性抗体,并按出生年份分层,以反映不同的早期 IAV 亚型暴露情况。选择参与者来检查对 H5 IAV 的全身和鼻腔抗体反应。
analysis_zh.methods: 分析血清和鼻腔样本中的 HA 特异性抗体,包括血清中和抗体、记忆 B 细胞群以及针对 H5 IAV 的鼻腔 IgG 和 IgA 滴度。测量抗体水平以评估预先存在的免疫力。
analysis_zh.main_results: 1957 年之前出生的个体表现出针对第 1 组 HA 抗原(包括 H5 和第 1 组 HA 干抗原)的最高现有血清抗体。然而,这些出生年份特异性模式并未反映在针对 H5 IAV 或 H5 特异性记忆 B 细胞群的血清中和抗体中。1957 年之前出生的个体中预先存在的 H5 鼻腔 IgG 和 IgA 滴度更高。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,生命早期接触造成的免疫偏差延伸到鼻粘膜(IAV 复制的主要部位)中检测到的抗体。这凸显了了解粘膜免疫在大流行防范中的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究表明,童年印记影响预先存在的对 H5 IAV 的粘膜免疫,这可能为针对大流行威胁的 监测 策略和 疫苗 设计提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其关注的是预先存在的抗体,并且没有涉及功能性免疫或针对感染的保护。证据是中等的,因为它依赖于横截面抽样并且没有建立因果关系。

papers.title: Some Exposure for Influenza Hemagglutinin Interface Antibodies.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza viruses are a constant threat to human health. Current vaccines often confer low to moderate protection against infection with seasonal viruses and little‐to‐no protection against pandemic viruses. Improved vaccines are needed. These vaccines will need to reliably elicit antibodies to conserved sites that are broadly protective. One strategy to do so is to design immunogens that present epitopes that are targeted by antibodies that are genetically similar, that humans have the genetic capacity to produce, and that are likely present in human naive B cell repertoires. Among the more recently described epitopes for broadly binding, protective antibodies are those on surfaces at protein–protein interfaces. This review will focus on describing many of these sites and the genetic features of antibodies that engage them. Interface epitopes are immunogenic, and antibodies to these sites are likely present in human repertoires following influenza infection or vaccination.

papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Influenza viruses are a constant threat to human health. Current vaccines often confer low to moderate protection against infection with seasonal viruses and little‐to‐no protection against pandemic viruses. Improved vaccines are needed. These vaccines will need to reliably elicit antibodies to conserved sites that are broadly protective. One strategy to do so is to design immunogens that present epitopes that are targeted by antibodies that are genetically similar, that humans have the genetic capacity to produce, and that are likely present in human naive B cell repertoires. Among the more recently described epitopes for broadly binding, protective antibodies are those on surfaces at protein–protein interfaces. This review will focus on describing many of these sites and the genetic features of antibodies that engage them. Interface epitopes are immunogenic, and antibodies to these sites are likely present in human repertoires following influenza infection or vaccination.

papers.title: Myth-busting influenza and fear of adverse reactions in healthcare workers: two experimental studies on vaccination intentions.
papers.abstract: Background Seasonal influenza causes significant global harms, and vaccinating healthcare workers (HCW) is central to protecting both staff and patients. However, HCW influenza vaccination rates remain below targets. Misconceptions, particularly concerns about adverse reactions, are frequently cited barriers, and many campaigns use myth-busting materials to counter these beliefs. This study tested whether correcting influenza myths and addressing concerns about adverse reactions leads to an increase in vaccine intentions. Methods Two online experimental studies were conducted. HCW participants were of primary interest but a general population sample was included for comparison. In Experiment 1 (HCW n = 514; general population n = 401), participants viewed images debunking common influenza myths, with randomisation to materials that either included or excluded an additional image addressing adverse reactions. Experiment 2 (HCW n = 535; general population n = 1200) focused exclusively on adverse reaction messaging, with participants randomised to one of four image formats. Vaccination intention was the primary outcome. Results In Experiment 1, myth-busting significantly increased vaccination intentions (all p 0.12) in both samples. Adding an adverse reactions image produced no additional increase. In Experiment 2, no overall effects emerged for HCW, but a significant interaction ( p = .011, ηp 2 = 0.04) indicated that effects varied by image: one increased intentions ( p = .029, d z = 0.25), two showed null effects, and one produced a marginal backfire effect ( p = .052 d z = −0.21). In the general population sample, intentions increased overall ( p < .001, d z = 0.15) with no interaction. Conclusions Vaccination intentions were reliably higher after viewing myth-busting materials than before, but control intentions were not. Myth-busting is therefore an effective approach to increasing influenza vaccination intentions. In contrast, explicitly addressing mild adverse reactions did not reliably raise intentions and, for one set of materials, marginally reduced them. Campaigns targeting HCW should therefore test adverse reaction messaging before implementation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the effectiveness of myth-busting materials in increasing influenza vaccination intentions among healthcare workers (HCW) and the general population. Two online experimental studies were conducted, with Experiment 1 testing myth-busting materials that included or excluded adverse reaction images, and Experiment 2 focusing solely on adverse reaction messaging. Results showed that myth-busting significantly increased vaccination intentions in both groups, while addressing adverse reactions had mixed effects. The study suggests that myth-busting is an effective strategy for improving vaccination intentions, but adverse reaction messaging should be tested before implementation. The findings have implications for public health campaigns aimed at increasing vaccine uptake, particularly among HCW.

papers.title_zh: 打破流感神话和医护人员对不良反应的恐惧:关于 疫苗接种 意图的两项实验研究。
papers.source_body_en: Background Seasonal influenza causes significant global harms, and vaccinating healthcare workers (HCW) is central to protecting both staff and patients. However, HCW influenza vaccination rates remain below targets. Misconceptions, particularly concerns about adverse reactions, are frequently cited barriers, and many campaigns use myth-busting materials to counter these beliefs. This study tested whether correcting influenza myths and addressing concerns about adverse reactions leads to an increase in vaccine intentions. Methods Two online experimental studies were conducted. HCW participants were of primary interest but a general population sample was included for comparison. In Experiment 1 (HCW n = 514; general population n = 401), participants viewed images debunking common influenza myths, with randomisation to materials that either included or excluded an additional image addressing adverse reactions. Experiment 2 (HCW n = 535; general population n = 1200) focused exclusively on adverse reaction messaging, with participants randomised to one of four image formats. Vaccination intention was the primary outcome. Results In Experiment 1, myth-busting significantly increased vaccination intentions (all p 0.12) in both samples. Adding an adverse reactions image produced no additional increase. In Experiment 2, no overall effects emerged for HCW, but a significant interaction ( p = .011, ηp 2 = 0.04) indicated that effects varied by image: one increased intentions ( p = .029, d z = 0.25), two showed null effects, and one produced a marginal backfire effect ( p = .052 d z = −0.21). In the general population sample, intentions increased overall ( p < .001, d z = 0.15) with no interaction. Conclusions Vaccination intentions were reliably higher after viewing myth-busting materials than before, but control intentions were not. Myth-busting is therefore an effective approach to increasing influenza vaccination intentions. In contrast, explicitly addressing mild adverse reactions did not reliably raise intentions and, for one set of materials, marginally reduced them. Campaigns targeting HCW should therefore test adverse reaction messaging before implementation.

papers.title: Influenza A H1N1 Infection Triggers Endothelial Immunothrombosis via TNF-α–Tissue Factor–Thrombin Signaling in Human Brain Microvascular Endothelial Cells
papers.abstract: Severe Influenza A virus (IAV) infection is associated with endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking endothelial inflammatory activation to thrombosis remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. We infected HBEC-5i cells with Influenza A/H1N1 pdm09. We assessed viral infection by RT-qPCR detection of matrix (M) transcripts and by immunoblotting for the M1 protein. We evaluated endothelial responses by measuring TNF-α expression and secretion, Tissue Factor (TF) expression, TF-dependent factor Xa generation, and responses to recombinant TNF-α and thrombin. H1N1 infection increased TNF-α expression and secretion and enhanced TF expression and functional activity, indicating acquisition of a procoagulant endothelial phenotype. Recombinant TNF-α reproduced infection-associated TF induction, whereas thrombin enhanced TNF-α production and TF activity, supporting reciprocal amplification between inflammatory and coagulation pathways. These findings support a TNF-α–TF–thrombin feed-forward signaling circuit linking endothelial inflammation and coagulation during H1N1 infection. Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, identifying this signaling axis as a potential mechanistic target for influenza-associated vascular and thrombotic complications.

papers.source_body_en: Severe Influenza A virus (IAV) infection is associated with endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking endothelial inflammatory activation to thrombosis remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. We infected HBEC-5i cells with Influenza A/H1N1 pdm09. We assessed viral infection by RT-qPCR detection of matrix (M) transcripts and by immunoblotting for the M1 protein. We evaluated endothelial responses by measuring TNF-α expression and secretion, Tissue Factor (TF) expression, TF-dependent factor Xa generation, and responses to recombinant TNF-α and thrombin. H1N1 infection increased TNF-α expression and secretion and enhanced TF expression and functional activity, indicating acquisition of a procoagulant endothelial phenotype. Recombinant TNF-α reproduced infection-associated TF induction, whereas thrombin enhanced TNF-α production and TF activity, supporting reciprocal amplification between inflammatory and coagulation pathways. These findings support a TNF-α–TF–thrombin feed-forward signaling circuit linking endothelial inflammation and coagulation during H1N1 infection. Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, identifying this signaling axis as a potential mechanistic target for influenza-associated vascular and thrombotic complications.
